title: 2007 HMMT February Geometry Problem 2
statement: \(A, B, C\), and \(D\) are points on a circle, and segments \(\overline{A C}\) and \(\overline{B D}\) intersect at \(P\), such that \(A P=8\), \(P C=1\), and \(B D=6\). Find \(B P\), given that \(B P<D P\).

solutions.text: 2. Writing \(B P=x\) and \(P D=6-x\), we have that \(B P<3\). Power of a point at \(P\) gives \(A P \cdot P C=B P \cdot P D\) or \(8=x(6-x)\). This can be solved for \(x=2\) and \(x=4\), and we discard the latter.
